Basic Training (Army doesn't have Boot Camp) is a pretty controlled atmosphere, there isn't a whole lot to see. You aren't allowed to leave campus, are monitored nearly 100% of the time, and the community is designed to have snitches all around (since everyone gets punished for the actions of a single soldier).

Not a lot of weird things happen. The guy who controls the toilet paper supply has all the power. I would make exchanges or buy TP with my meager income, and could get anything I wanted. Those who snuck in porn, tobacco, caffeine, or any other banned substance didn't necessarily plan for the future too well. So I was able to get any of that stuff when I wanted it, without having to store it and getting caught. Toilet paper is powerful.

There were no doors on the stalls. I thought that was weird and took some getting used to. I take that back, there was one stall with a door. We called it the Masturbation Station. Looking back, it was probably designed for that purpose.

This guy from Africa flipped the fuck out and tried to attack the drill sergeant. He got punched right in the chest, fell to the ground, the sergeant grabbed him by the collar, drug him across the snot, vomit, and tear covered floor, and literally threw him out the door like a cartoon.
